life: Annual or biennial, 1–2 ft, glaucous blue-green foliage
edible_parts: None — the plant contains isoquinoline alkaloids and is not edible.
other_uses: A pioneer of rocky outcrops, burned ground and other disturbed sites; pink-and-yellow flowers are worked by bumblebees and visited by hummingbirds. Useful for colonising thin, poor soils where little else establishes.
harvest: Not harvested for food. Collect seed in summer if propagating.
soil: Dry, rocky, sharply drained, often acidic; poor soils suit it.
risks: TOXIC. Like other Papaveraceae it carries isoquinoline alkaloids; ingestion can cause nervous-system effects in people and livestock. Grow it for habitat and its flowers, never for food.
buy: Occasionally offered by specialist native nurseries; usually grown from seed. Also listed under its accepted name Capnoides sempervirens.
